sentences.zh: 梁書卷第十 列傳第四

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 10, Biographies 4
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume Ten, Biographies, Fourth

sentences.zh: 蕭穎達 夏侯詳 蔡道恭 楊公則 鄧元起

translations.literal: Xiao Yingda; Xia Hou Xiang; Cai Daogong; Yang Gongze; Deng Yuanqi
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingda; Xia Hou Xiang; Cai Daogong; Yang Gongze; Deng Yuanqi

sentences.zh: 蕭穎達，蘭陵蘭陵人，齊光祿大夫赤斧第五子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Yingda was a native of Lanling in Lanling commandery, the fifth son of Qi's Grandee of the Imperial Secretariat Chi Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingda came from Lanling in Lanling commandery, the fifth son of Qi Grandee of the Imperial Secretariat Chi Fu.

sentences.zh: 少好勇使氣，起家冠軍。

translations.literal: In youth he loved boldness and thrived on bravado; he first entered office as Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved daring and thrived on bravado; he began his career as Champion General.

sentences.zh: 兄穎胄，齊建武末行荊州事，穎達亦爲西中郎外兵參軍，俱在西府。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yingzhou in late Qi's Jianwu era administered Jing province affairs; Yingda also served as aide to the minister of war of the Western Zhonglang General, both at the western headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yingzhou, in late Qi's Jianwu era, ran Jing province; Yingda too was aide to the Western Zhonglang General's minister of war, both in the western command.

sentences.zh: 齊季多難，頗不自安。

translations.literal: In Qi's troubled final years they were quite ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi's closing troubles they felt deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 會東昏遣輔國將軍劉山陽爲巴西太守，道過荊州，密敕穎胄襲雍州。

translations.literal: Then Emperor Donghun dispatched Supporting-the-State General Liu Shanyang as Administrator of Brazil; passing Jingzhou, he secretly instructed Yingzhou to seize Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun then sent Supporting-the-State General Liu Shanyang to Brazil as administrator; on the road through Jingzhou he secretly ordered Yingzhou to strike Yong province.

sentences.zh: 時高祖已爲備矣。

translations.literal: By then Gaozu had already made his preparations.
translations.idiomatic: By then Gaozu had already prepared.

sentences.zh: 仍遣穎胄親人王天虎以書疑之。

translations.literal: He therefore sent Yingzhou's kinsman Wang Tianhu with a letter to sow doubt.
translations.idiomatic: So he sent Yingzhou's kinsman Wang Tianhu with a letter meant to unsettle him.

sentences.zh: 山陽至，果不敢入城。

translations.literal: When Shanyang arrived, he truly dared not enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanyang arrived, he in fact dared not enter the city.

sentences.zh: 穎胄計無所出，夜遣錢塘人朱景思呼西中郎城局參軍席闡文、諮議參軍柳忱閉齋定議。

translations.literal: Yingzhou, with no plan at hand, at night sent the man of Qiantang Zhu Jingsi to summon Western Zhonglang headquarters adjutant Xi Wenkai and advisory officer Liu Chen to close the study and fix a decision.
translations.idiomatic: At a loss, Yingzhou by night sent Zhu Jingsi of Qiantang to call Xi Wenkai, the headquarters adjutant of the Western Zhonglang General, and advisory officer Liu Chen to shut the study and settle on a course.

sentences.zh: 闡文曰：「蕭雍州蓄養士馬，非復一日，江陵素畏襄陽人，人衆又不敵，取之必不可制，制之，歲寒復不爲朝廷所容。

translations.literal: Xi Wenkai said: "The Lord of Yong province has been raising men and horses for no single day; Jiangling has always feared men of Xiangyang, and their numbers are not a match—we cannot take them and be sure of control; even if controlled, when the year turns cold they will again not be tolerated by the court.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Wenkai said: "The Yongzhou lord has been gathering troops and horses for ages; Jiangling has always feared Xiangyang men, and their numbers cannot match—seize them and you cannot hold them; hold them, and when winter comes the court will not abide it again.

sentences.zh: 今若殺山陽，與雍州舉事，立天子以令諸侯，則霸業成矣。

translations.literal: If we now kill Shanyang and rise with Yong province, set up the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords, then hegemony will be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Kill Shanyang now, rise with Yongzhou, set up the Son of Heaven to command the lords, and hegemony is won.

sentences.zh: 山陽持疑不進，是不信我。

translations.literal: Shanyang holds back in doubt and does not advance—this is that he does not trust us.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang hesitates and will not advance—that means he does not trust us.

sentences.zh: 今斬送天虎，則彼疑可釋。

translations.literal: If we now cut off Tianhu's head and present it, his suspicions can be dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off Tianhu's head and send it now, and his doubts can be cleared.

sentences.zh: 至而圖之，罔不濟矣。

translations.literal: When he arrives we plot against him—nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: When he comes, strike—nothing will fail.

sentences.zh: 」忱亦勸焉。

translations.literal: " Chen also urged it.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen urged the same.

sentences.zh: 穎達曰：「善。

translations.literal: Yingda said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Yingda said: "Good."

sentences.zh: 」及天明，穎胄謂天虎曰：「卿與劉輔國相識，今不得不借卿頭。

translations.literal: When dawn came, Yingzhou told Tianhu: "You are acquainted with the Supporting-the-State Liu; today I cannot but borrow your head."
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Yingzhou told Tianhu: "You know the Supporting-the-State Liu; today I must borrow your head."

sentences.zh: 」乃斬天虎以示山陽。

translations.literal: He then beheaded Tianhu and displayed him to Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Tianhu and showed the head to Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 山陽大喜，輕將步騎數百到州。

translations.literal: Shanyang was greatly pleased; lightly he led several hundred infantry and cavalry to the province.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang rejoiced; with only a few hundred foot and horse he came to the provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 闡文勒兵待於門，山陽車踰限而門闔，因執斬之，傳首高祖。

translations.literal: Wenkai drew up troops waiting at the gate; Shanyang's carriage crossed the gate limit and the gates closed; they seized and beheaded him, sent the head to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkai had troops wait at the gate; Shanyang's carriage passed the gate-bar and the gates shut; they seized and killed him and sent his head to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 且以奉南康王之議來告，高祖許焉。

translations.literal: And with the plan to enthrone the Prince of Nankang they came to report; Gaozu assented.
translations.idiomatic: They also reported the plan to enthrone the Prince of Nankang; Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 和帝卽位，以穎胄爲假節、侍中、尚書令、領吏部尚書、都督行留諸軍事、鎮軍將軍、荊州刺史，留衛西朝。

translations.literal: When Emperor He took the throne, Yingzhou was made Acting-with-credentials, Palace Attendant, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, concurrently Director of the Imperial Secretariat for Official Affairs, Superintendent of military affairs remaining and departing, General Who Tranquilizes the Army, Governor of Jingzhou, remaining to guard the Western court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He ascended, Yingzhou became Acting-with-credentials, Palace Attendant, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Director for Official Affairs, superintendent of armies staying and going, General Who Tranquilizes the Army, and governor of Jingzhou, left to guard the western court.

sentences.zh: 以穎達爲冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Yingda was made Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: Yingda was made Champion General.

sentences.zh: 及楊公則等率師隨高祖，高祖圍郢城，穎達會軍於漢口，與王茂、曹景宗等攻郢城，陷之。

translations.literal: When Yang Gongze and the rest led troops with Gaozu, Gaozu besieged Ying city; Yingda joined the army at Hankou and with Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, and the rest attacked Ying city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Gongze and others marched with Gaozu, Gaozu besieged Ying; Yingda met the host at Hankou and with Wang Mao and Cao Jingzong attacked Ying and captured it.

sentences.zh: 隨高祖平江州。

translations.literal: He followed Gaozu in pacifying Jiang province.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gaozu in pacifying Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 高祖進江州，使與曹景宗先率馬步進趨江寧，破東昏將李居士，又下東城。

translations.literal: Gaozu advanced into Jiang province and sent him with Cao Jingzong to lead horse and foot first toward Jiangning, defeated Emperor Donghun's general Li Jushi, and again took the eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu entered Jiang province and sent him with Cao Jingzong ahead with cavalry and infantry toward Jiangning; they broke Emperor Donghun's general Li Jushi and took the eastern city.

sentences.zh: 初，義師之起也，巴東太守蕭惠訓子璝、巴西太守魯休烈弗從，舉兵侵荊州，敗輔國將軍任漾之於硤口，破大將軍劉孝慶於上明，穎胄遣軍拒之；

translations.literal: At the start, when the righteous army rose, Baodong Administrator Xiao Huixun's son Gui and Brazil Administrator Lu Xiulie would not follow; they raised troops and invaded Jing province, defeated Supporting-the-State General Ren Yangzhi at Xiakou, broke Grand General Liu Xiaoqing at Shangming, and Yingzhou sent troops to resist them;
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army first rose, Xiao Gui, son of Baodong administrator Xiao Huixun, and Brazil administrator Lu Xiulie refused obedience; they invaded Jing province, defeated Supporting-the-State General Ren Yangzhi at Xiakou and Grand General Liu Xiaoqing at Shangming, and Yingzhou sent armies against them;

sentences.zh: 而高祖已平江、郢，圖建康。

translations.literal: but Gaozu had already pacified Jiang and Ying and was plotting Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: but Gaozu had already taken Jiang and Ying and turned toward Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 穎胄自以職居上將，不能拒制璝等，憂愧不樂，發疾數日而卒。

translations.literal: Yingzhou, holding the highest command, could not check Gui and the rest; grieving and ashamed, he fell ill and died within days.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou, as supreme commander, could not contain Gui and the others; sick with shame and grief, he died after several days' illness.

sentences.zh: 州中秘之，使似其書者假爲教命。

translations.literal: The province kept it secret and had someone whose hand resembled his forge orders as if from him.
translations.idiomatic: The province concealed it and had a man with a similar hand write orders in his name.

sentences.zh: 及璝等聞建康將平，衆懼而潰，乃始發喪，和帝贈穎胄丞相。

translations.literal: When Gui and the rest heard Jiankang would soon be pacified, the host feared and scattered; only then did they hold mourning, and Emperor He posthumously made Yingzhou Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui and the others heard Jiankang was about to fall, their forces broke in fear; only then was mourning declared, and Emperor He posthumously made Yingzhou chancellor.

sentences.zh: 義師初，穎達弟穎孚自京師出亡，廬陵人循景智潛引與南歸，至廬陵，景智及宗人靈祐爲起兵，得數百人，屯西昌藥山湖。

translations.literal: At the start of the righteous army Yingda's younger brother Yingfu fled the capital; the man of Luling Xun Jingzhi secretly guided him south; reaching Luling, Jingzhi and kinsman Ling You raised troops and mustered several hundred men, encamped at Yaoshan Lake in Xichang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the righteous rising Yingda's brother Yingfu escaped the capital; Xun Jingzhi of Luling secretly led him south; at Luling, Jingzhi and kinsman Ling You raised troops—several hundred men at Yaoshan Lake in Xichang.

sentences.zh: 穎達聞之，假穎孚節、督廬陵豫章臨川南康安成五郡軍事、冠軍將軍、廬陵內史。

translations.literal: When Yingda heard, he gave Yingfu acting credentials as superintendent of the military affairs of the five commanderies Luling, Yuzhang, Linchuan, Nankang, and Ancheng, Champion General, and Interior Administrator of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Yingda heard and gave Yingfu acting credentials as superintendent of Luling, Yuzhang, Linchuan, Nankang, and Ancheng, Champion General, and interior administrator of Luling.

sentences.zh: 穎孚率靈祐等進據西昌，東昏遣安西太守劉希祖自南江入湖拒之。

translations.literal: Yingfu led Ling You and the rest forward to hold Xichang; Emperor Donghun dispatched Pacified West Administrator Liu Xizu from the southern river into the lake to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Yingfu advanced with Ling You to hold Xichang; Emperor Donghun sent Pacified West administrator Liu Xizu from the southern river into the lake against him.

sentences.zh: 穎孚不能自立，以其兵由建安復奔長沙，希祖追之，穎孚緣山踰嶂，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Yingfu could not hold; he led his troops through Jian'an back toward Changsha, Xizu pursued, and Yingfu crossed ridges and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yingfu could not stand; he led his men through Jian'an toward Changsha while Xizu pursued; Yingfu crossed mountains and ridges and barely survived.

sentences.zh: 在道絕糧，後因食過飽而卒。

translations.literal: On the road they ran out of food; later he died from eating too much.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they starved; later he died from eating too much at once.

sentences.zh: 建康城平，高祖以穎達爲前將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Gaozu made Yingda Front Army General and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell, Gaozu made Yingda Front Army General and governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 上受禪，詔曰：「念功惟德，列代所同，追遠懷人，彌與事篤。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the mandate, an edict said: "To mark merit is to esteem virtue, alike in every age; to follow the distant and cherish the departed is all the more bound to the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, an edict said: "To honor merit is to esteem virtue, the same in every age; to reach back and cherish the dead binds one all the more to the task.

sentences.zh: 齊故侍中、丞相、尚書令穎胄，風格峻遠，器㝢深邵，清猷盛業，問望斯歸。

translations.literal: Former Qi Palace Attendant, Chancellor, and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yingzhou—his bearing lofty and far, his capacity deep and broad, his pure designs and grand achievements, his reputation and gaze turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qi palace attendant, chancellor, and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yingzhou—bearing lofty and distant, capacity deep and broad, pure designs and great deeds, fame and expectation alike upon him.

sentences.zh: 締構義始，肇基王迹，契闊屯夷，載形心事。

translations.literal: He joined the righteous beginning, laid the foundation of the royal trace, shared hardship in tumult and peace, and carried his heart's affairs in the record.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the righteous start, laid the royal foundation, shared hardship through turmoil and peace, and bore his heart on the record.

sentences.zh: 朕膺天改物，光宅區宇，望岱觀河，永言號慟。

translations.literal: We have received Heaven, changed the realm, and lit the dwelling of the four quarters; gazing at Mount Tai and viewing the River, forever we speak in lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: We have received Heaven, changed the realm, and settled the four quarters; gazing at Mount Tai and viewing the River, we lament without end.

sentences.zh: 可封巴東郡開國公，食邑三千戶，本官如故。

translations.literal: He may be enfeoffed Duke of Baxi commandery, fief of three thousand households, his former office unchanged."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be enfeoffed Duke of Baxi commandery with a fief of three thousand households, his former rank unchanged."

sentences.zh: 」贈穎孚右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yingfu was posthumously made Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Yingfu was posthumously made Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 加穎達散騎常侍，以公事免。

translations.literal: Yingda was added as Secular Attendant; he was dismissed for official business.
translations.idiomatic: Yingda was added as Secular Attendant; he was removed for official business.

sentences.zh: 及大論功賞，封穎達吳昌縣侯，邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: When merits were broadly debated and rewarded, Yingda was enfeoffed Marquis of Wuchang county, fief fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the great merit review Yingda was enfeoffed Marquis of Wuchang county with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋爲侍中，改封作唐侯，縣邑如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was Palace Attendant, changed to Marquis of Zuotang, fief unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was palace attendant, re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Zuotang with the same fief.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍、太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Left Guard of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Left Guard of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞任昉奏曰：

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞貧觀所取，窮視不爲。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in poverty one observes what one takes; in extremity what one will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that poverty shows what one will take; extremity shows what one will not do.

sentences.zh: 在於布衣，窮居介然之行，尚可以激貪厲俗，惇此薄夫；

translations.literal: Among men in plain cloth, conduct firm in humble dwelling can yet stir greed and sharpen custom, giving heart to thin men;
translations.idiomatic: Among commoners, conduct steadfast in a poor house can still stir greed and sharpen custom and give heart to petty men;

sentences.zh: 況乎伐冰之家，爭雞豚之利；

translations.literal: how much more houses that chop ice, contending for the profit of chickens and pigs;
translations.idiomatic: how much more in houses that break ice, contending for pig-and-chicken profit;

sentences.zh: 衣繡之士，受賈人之服。

translations.literal: men in embroidered robes accepting a merchant's garment.
translations.idiomatic: men in embroidered robes taking a merchant's gift.

sentences.zh: 風聞征虜將軍臣蕭穎達啓乞魚軍稅，輒攝穎達宅督彭難當到臺辨問。

translations.literal: We hear that General Who Punishes the Barbarians your servant Yingda memorialized begging fish-army tax; I took and summoned household supervisor Peng Nandang of Yingda's residence to the bureau for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: We hear that General Who Punishes the Barbarians, your servant Yingda, petitioned for fish-office tax; I summoned Yingda's household supervisor Peng Nandang to the bureau for inquiry.

sentences.zh: 列稱『尋生魚典稅，先本是鄧僧琰啓乞，限訖今年五月十四日。

translations.literal: He set forth: 'The live-fish office tax was originally memorialized by Deng Sengyan, term ending this year on the fourteenth day of the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: 'The live-fish office tax was first petitioned by Deng Sengyan, its term ending this year on the fourteenth day of the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 主人穎達，于時謂非新立，仍啓乞接代僧琰，卽蒙降許登稅，與史法論一年收直五十萬。

translations.literal: The master Yingda, deeming it not newly established, still memorialized to succeed Sengyan and at once received decree permitting levy; with the clerk-law they reckoned one year's receipts at five hundred thousand.' As the listed account, it matches the report heard; Yingda is master.
translations.idiomatic: Master Yingda, holding it no new levy, still petitioned to succeed Sengyan and at once received permission to register the tax; by clerk-law one year's take was five hundred thousand.' As set forth, it matches what was heard; Yingda is the principal.

sentences.zh: 』如其列狀，則與風聞符同，穎達卽主。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully reviews: General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Left Guard of the Heir Apparent, Marquis of Zuotang county, your servant Yingda—fills a minister's seat, heard in law-enforcement, private petitions repeatedly presented, utmost publicness lonely.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully finds: General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Left Guard of the Heir Apparent, Marquis of Zuotang, your servant Yingda—holds a minister's place, privy to enforcement of law, yet private suits crowd in while public duty stands empty.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案：征虜將軍、太子左衛率、作唐縣開國侯臣穎達，備位大臣，預聞執憲，私謁亟陳，至公寂寞。

translations.literal: Ambition in the butcher's stall, unlike seeking in Bao's market;
translations.idiomatic: Ambition in the butcher's stall, not like seeking in Bao's market;

sentences.zh: 屠中之志，異乎鮑肆之求；

translations.literal: fish-meal funds, not awaiting secretly existing numbers.
translations.idiomatic: fish-ration revenue, not waiting on hidden tallies.

sentences.zh: 魚飧之資，不俟潛有之數。

translations.literal: Then again he presented this document twice, pursued that eleven—if style is thus, the measure is here!
translations.idiomatic: Yet again he filed this text twice, chasing that eleven—if the manner is such, the cord is here!

sentences.zh: 遂復申茲文二，追彼十一，風體若茲，準繩斯在！

translations.literal: Your Majesty magnanimously cherishes meritorious good, each time bending law;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, in mercy for the meritorious, often bends the law;

sentences.zh: 陛下弘惜勳良，每爲曲法；

translations.literal: your servant holding office enforcing law, dares not not straighten the cord.
translations.idiomatic: your servant, holding office and enforcing law, dares not fail to draw the line straight.

sentences.zh: 臣當官執憲，敢不直繩。

translations.literal: Your servants collectively deliberate: request by the present matter to dismiss Yingda from his offices held, return the marquis to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: We jointly recommend: by the facts before us, remove Yingda from his posts and send the marquis home.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，請以見事免穎達所居官，以侯還第。

translations.literal: There was an edict pardoning him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 有詔原之。

translations.literal: He was transferred Secular Attendant, Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Secular Attendant and Left Guard General.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍、左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Soon again Palace Attendant, Commandant of the Court for the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again palace attendant and Commandant of the Court for the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 俄復爲侍中，衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He went out as Trustworthy-and-Awesome General, Interior Administrator of Yuzhang, added salary at the rank of two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Trustworthy-and-Awesome General and interior administrator of Yuzhang, with added salary at two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 出爲信威將軍、豫章內史，加秩中二千石。

translations.literal: His governance was fierce and harsh; the commandery people feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with fierce severity; the people of the commandery feared him.

sentences.zh: 治任威猛，郡人畏之。

translations.literal: He was promoted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Superintendent of the military affairs of Jiang province, Governor of Jiang province, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Bearer of the Staff, superintendent of Jiang province military affairs, and governor of Jiang province, with his generalship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 遷使持節、都督江州諸軍事、江州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Regular Attendant at the Court, Right Valiant Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned as Regular Attendant at the Court and Right Valiant Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 頃之，徵爲通直散騎常侍、右驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Having attained easy leisure, he especially indulged in sound and color, drank wine past measure, and by this somewhat harmed his life.
translations.idiomatic: Once at ease in high rank, he gave himself especially to music and women, drank beyond measure, and by this injured his health.

sentences.zh: 旣處優閑，尤恣聲色，飲酒過度，頗以此傷生。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was moved to Trustworthy-and-Awesome General, Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made Trustworthy-and-Awesome General and Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷信威將軍、右衛將軍。

translations.literal: That year he died, age thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died, aged thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 是歲卒，年三十四。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage came to mourn; given Eastern Garden secret objects, one set court robes, one suit clothing, money twenty myriad, cloth two hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn; he was given Eastern Garden funeral goods, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, two hundred thousand cash, and two hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨哭，給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢二十萬，布二百匹。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant and Central Guard General, with one set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、中衛將軍，鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Kang.

sentences.zh: 諡曰康。

translations.literal: Son Min succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min inherited.

sentences.zh: 子敏嗣。

translations.literal: Yingzhou's son Mi inherited Duke of Baxi, reached Attendant of the Central Court, died young.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou's son Mi inherited the Duke of Baxi, rose to Attendant of the Central Court, and died young.

sentences.zh: 穎胄子靡，襲巴東公，位至中書郎，早卒。

translations.literal: Xia Hou Xiang, styled Shuye, was a native of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Hou Xiang, styled Shuye, came from Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 夏侯詳，字叔業，譙郡人也。

translations.literal: At sixteen he met his father's death; in mourning he was grief-stricken and wasted.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he lost his father; in mourning he was broken with grief.

sentences.zh: 年十六，遭父艱，居喪哀毀。

translations.literal: Three years he dwelt at the tomb; once a three-legged sparrow flew to perch on his hut door—all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: For three years he lived at the tomb; once a three-legged sparrow flew to his hut door—all thought it strange.

sentences.zh: 三年廬于墓，嘗有雀三足，飛來集其廬戶，衆咸異焉。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Governor Yin Yan summoned him to fill chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Governor Yin Yan called him to serve as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 服闋，刺史殷琰召補主簿。

translations.literal: Early in Song's Taishi, Yan raised Yuzhou in revolt; Emperor Ming sent Supporting-the-State General Liu Le to attack; attack and defense continued months; men's hearts were fearful and they would ask aid from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Song's Taishi, Yan rebelled in Yuzhou; Emperor Ming sent Supporting-the-State General Liu Le to suppress him; siege and defense dragged on for months, hearts were afraid, and they would seek help from Wei.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，琰舉豫州叛，宋明帝遣輔國將軍劉勔討之，攻守連月，人情危懼，將請救於魏。

translations.literal: Xiang told Yan: "Today's undertaking, originally is to effect loyal fidelity;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said to Yan: "This rising was meant from the first to prove loyal duty;

sentences.zh: 詳說琰曰：「今日之舉，本效忠節；

translations.literal: if the altars have support, then return the body to the court—how can one bow the body north to an alien land.
translations.idiomatic: if the altars have a master, let us return to the court—how bow north to an alien realm?

sentences.zh: 若社稷有奉，便歸身朝廷，何可屈身北面異域。

translations.literal: Moreover today's Wei troops are close at Huai bank; one army has not measured going or staying, we fear there is alien plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Wei's troops are now on the Huai; one army has not yet shown its intent, and we fear treachery.

sentences.zh: 且今魏氏之卒，近在淮次，一軍未測去就，懼有異圖。

translations.literal: If now we send an envoy to return allegiance, they will surely thickly comfort and receive—not only exempt from crime.
translations.idiomatic: If we send envoys to submit now, they will surely receive us generously—not only pardon.

sentences.zh: 今若遣使歸款，必厚相慰納，豈止免罪而已。

translations.literal: If you say it is not so, your servant begs to serve as one envoy."
translations.idiomatic: If you doubt it, your servant begs to go as envoy."

sentences.zh: 若謂不然，請充一介。

translations.literal: Yan assented.
translations.idiomatic: Yan agreed.

sentences.zh: 」琰許之。

translations.literal: Xiang saw Le and said: "General, your strict encirclement, precipitous ramparts, arrows and blades like frost; within the city fools are truly like trapped beasts; gentry and common fear execution, all wish to turn to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang saw Le and said: "General, your tight siege and steep walls, arrows and blades like frost—the fools in the city are trapped beasts; gentry and commoners fear death and all wish to turn to Wei.

sentences.zh: 詳見勔曰：「將軍嚴圍峭壘，矢刃如霜，城內愚徒，實同困獸，士庶懼誅，咸欲投魏。

translations.literal: Your servant therefore crossed the wall to return virtue, dares spread the belly's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant crossed the wall to yield—this is my inmost heart laid bare.

sentences.zh: 僕所以逾城歸德，敢布腹心。

translations.literal: I wish the General would extend vast liberal grace, let fall generous favor, lift siege and withdraw camp—then all will lead one another and come.
translations.idiomatic: I beg the General to grant vast mercy and generous favor, lift the siege and withdraw—then all will come out together.

sentences.zh: 願將軍弘曠蕩之恩，垂霈然之惠，解圍退舍，則皆相率而至矣。

translations.literal: " Le assented.
translations.idiomatic: " Le agreed.

sentences.zh: 」勔許之。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Examining this, it shall be as you say; yet Xiang begs to return with orders.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said: "If it is truly so, it shall be as you say; but your servant begs leave to report back.

sentences.zh: 詳曰：「審爾，當如君言，而詳請反命。

translations.literal: " Le sent him to the wall foot; Xiang called to the people within, spoke Le's words; that same day Yan and the multitude all came out; the whole province was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: " Le sent him to the foot of the wall; Xiang called to those within and told them Le's words; that same day Yan and all the host came out, and the whole province was saved.

sentences.zh: 」勔遣到城下，詳呼城中人，語以勔辭，卽日琰及衆俱出，一州以全。

translations.literal: Le became governor, again supplemented chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Le became governor and again made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 勔爲刺史，又補主簿。

translations.literal: Before long he was magistrate of Xingji, administration had unusual achievement; Governor Duan Furong circulated within the border, making a model for subordinate prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was magistrate of Xingji, with outstanding administration; Governor Duan Furong circulated his record within the jurisdiction as a model for subordinate prefectures.

sentences.zh: 頃之，爲新汲令，治有異績，刺史段佛榮班下境內，爲屬城表。

translations.literal: He was transferred Senior Recorder, then promoted Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Senior Recorder, then promoted Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 轉治中從事史，仍遷別駕。

translations.literal: He was transferred Senior Recorder, then promoted Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Senior Recorder, then promoted Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 歷事八將，州部稱之。

translations.literal: He had served eight generals, and the province and commandery praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He served eight commanders in turn, and the province spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝爲刺史，雅相器遇。

translations.literal: When Qi Mingdi was inspector, he greatly favored and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Mingdi held the inspectorship, he singled Xiang out for favor.

sentences.zh: 及輔政，招令出都，將大用之。

translations.literal: When Mingdi became regent, he summoned him to the capital, intending to employ him in great matters.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the regency, he called Xiang to the capital for a major appointment.

sentences.zh: 每引詳及鄉人裴叔業日夜與語，詳輒末略不酬。

translations.literal: Each night he would draw Xiang and his fellow townsman Pei Shuye into long talk; Xiang would always answer vaguely and not engage.
translations.idiomatic: Nightly he drew Xiang and Pei Shuye into conversation; Xiang would murmur and not truly reply.

sentences.zh: 帝以問叔業，叔業告詳。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Shuye, and Shuye reported what Xiang had said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Shuye, and Shuye repeated Xiang's words.

sentences.zh: 詳曰：「不爲福始，不爲禍先。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Do not be the first to bring good fortune; do not be the first to bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Do not be first to court fortune, nor first to invite ruin.

sentences.zh: 」由此微有忤。

translations.literal: " From this there was a slight offense.
translations.idiomatic: " From that moment he fell slightly out of favor.

sentences.zh: 出爲征虜長史、義陽太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Chief Clerk for the Campaign against the Barbarians and Administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as chief clerk on the campaign-against-barbarians staff and administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 頃之、建安戍爲魏所圍，仍以詳爲建安戍主，帶邊城、新蔡二郡太守，幷督光城、弋陽、汝陰三郡衆赴之。

translations.literal: Before long the Jian'an garrison was besieged by Wei; Xiang was again made commandant of Jian'an, concurrently Administrator of Biancheng and Xincai, and ordered to lead the forces of Guangcheng, Yiyang, and Ruyin to its relief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Jian'an garrison was surrounded by Wei; Xiang was again made its commandant, with Biancheng and Xincai, and led troops from Guangcheng, Yiyang, and Ruyin to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 詳至建安，魏軍引退。

translations.literal: When Xiang reached Jian'an, the Wei army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang reached Jian'an and the Wei forces pulled back.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏又於淮上置荊亭戍，常爲寇掠，累攻不能禦，詳率銳卒攻之，賊衆大潰，皆棄城奔走。

translations.literal: Earlier Wei had set up Jingting garrison on the Huai, which constantly raided; repeated attacks could not stop them; Xiang led crack troops against it, the bandits were utterly routed, and all abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had built Jingting garrison on the Huai as a raiding base; repeated strikes failed to break it until Xiang led elite troops, routed the enemy, and drove them from the walls.

sentences.zh: 建武末，征爲遊擊將軍，出爲南中郎司馬、南新蔡太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwu he was summoned as General of Mobile Columns and sent out as Major of the Southern Gentlemen of the Palace and Administrator of Southern Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianwu he was recalled as general of mobile columns and sent out as southern palace major and administrator of Southern Xincai.

sentences.zh: 齊南康王爲荊州，遷西中郎司馬、新興太守，便道先到江陽。

translations.literal: When the Qi Prince of Nankang held Jingzhou, Xiang was transferred to Major of the Western Gentlemen and Administrator of Xinxing; he took a shortcut and reached Jiangyang first.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Nankang took Jingzhou, Xiang became western palace major and administrator of Xinxing and, by a direct route, reached Jiangyang ahead of the rest.

sentences.zh: 時始安王遙光稱兵京邑，南康王長史蕭穎胄並未至，中兵參軍劉山陽先在州，山陽副潘紹欲謀作亂，詳偽呼紹議事，卽於城門斬之，州府乃安。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang had raised troops in the capital; the Nankang Prince's chief clerk Xiao Yinggou had not yet arrived; Army Aide Liu Shanyang was already in the province; Shanyang's deputy Pan Shao wished to plot rebellion; Xiang feigned calling Shao to discuss affairs and at once beheaded him at the city gate—the province and headquarters were then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang had risen in the capital; Yinggou had not yet reached the province; Liu Shanyang was already there, and his deputy Pan Shao meant to rebel; Xiang lured Shao to the gate on pretense of counsel and cut off his head, and the province was secured.

sentences.zh: 遷司州刺史，辭不之職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Sizhou but declined and did not take the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered Sizhou but refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 高祖義兵起，詳與穎胄同創大舉。

translations.literal: When Gaozu's righteous army rose, Xiang and Yinggou together launched the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised the righteous army, Xiang and Yinggou opened the great undertaking together.

sentences.zh: 西臺建，以詳爲中領軍，加散騎常侍、南郡太守。

translations.literal: When the Western Headquarters was established, Xiang was made Central Army Commander, with the additional titles Regular Attendant and Administrator of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: With the Western Headquarters in being, Xiang became central army commander, also regular attendant and administrator of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 凡軍國大事，穎胄多決於詳。

translations.literal: On all military and state affairs, Yinggou largely decided through Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In military and civil matters alike, Yinggou leaned on Xiang for judgment.

sentences.zh: 及高祖圍郢城未下，穎胄遣衛尉席闡文如高祖軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu besieged Ying city without taking it, Yinggou sent Minister of Ceremonies Xi Chayan to Gaozu's army.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu still held Ying city under siege, Yinggou sent Xi Chayan, minister of ceremonies, to his camp.

sentences.zh: 詳獻議曰：「窮壁易守，攻取勢難；

translations.literal: Xiang submitted a plan: "A desperate wall is easy to hold; to assault and take it is strategically difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang offered counsel: "A cornered city holds easily; to storm it is the harder course.

sentences.zh: 頓甲堅城，兵家所忌。

translations.literal: to stall armor before a stout city is what military strategists dread.
translations.idiomatic: To pin an army before strong walls is what every strategist warns against.

sentences.zh: 誠宜大弘經略，詢納羣言。

translations.literal: Truly one ought greatly to broaden strategy and inquire into and accept the counsel of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: You should widen the plan and gather every voice.

sentences.zh: 軍主以下至於匹夫，皆令獻其所見，盡其所懷，擇善而從，選能而用，不以人廢言，不以多罔寡。

translations.literal: From army commanders down to common men, all should be made to offer what they see and express all they think; choose the good and follow it, select the able and employ them; do not reject words because of the person, do not let numbers obscure the few.
translations.idiomatic: From generals to common soldiers, let each speak his mind; take what is sound, use who is fit, and never silence a good word for its speaker nor drown the few in the many.

sentences.zh: 又須量我衆力，度賊樵糧，窺彼人情，權其形勢。

translations.literal: One must also measure our multitude's strength, gauge the enemy's firewood and grain, spy on their human sentiment, and weigh their disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh our numbers, measure their fuel and grain, read their hearts, and judge their position.

sentences.zh: 若使賊人衆而食少，故宜計日而守之；

translations.literal: If the enemy are many but food is scant, then one should plan to hold out by the day;
translations.idiomatic: If they are many and hungry, count the days and hold;

sentences.zh: 食多而力寡，故宜悉衆而攻之。

translations.literal: if food is abundant but strength is thin, then one should concentrate all forces and attack.
translations.idiomatic: if they are well fed but few, mass every man and strike.

sentences.zh: 若使糧力俱足，非攻守所屈，便宜散金寶，縱反間，使彼智者不用，愚者懷猜，此魏武之所以定大業也。

translations.literal: If grain and strength are both sufficient so that neither assault nor defense can break them, then one should scatter gold and jewels and set loose double agents, so that their wise are not used and their fools harbor suspicion—this is how Wei Wu established the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: If grain and arms are both ample and neither siege nor assault will bend them, scatter gold and sow distrust until the clever are ignored and the foolish turn on one another—that is how Cao Cao won an empire.

sentences.zh: 若三事未可，宜思變通，觀於人情，計我糧穀。

translations.literal: If none of the three courses is feasible, one should think of shifts and expedients, observe human sentiment, and reckon our grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: If none of these three paths will serve, seek another way, watch the mood of men, and count our stores.

sentences.zh: 若德之所感，萬里同符，仁之所懷，遠邇歸義，金帛素積，糧運又充，乃可以列圍寬守，引以歲月，此王翦之所以剋楚也。

translations.literal: If where virtue moves the ten thousand li answer in accord, and where benevolence dwells near and far return to righteousness, with gold and silk long accumulated and grain transport again full—then one may array siege lines and hold loosely, drawing it out by months and years; this is how Wang Jian conquered Chu.
translations.idiomatic: If virtue draws the realm to you and benevolence gathers the distant, with treasure hoarded and convoys full, then ring the walls and wait the seasons out, as Wang Jian broke Chu.

sentences.zh: 若圍之不卒降，攻之未可下，間道不能行，金粟無人積，天下非一家，人情難可豫，此則宜更思變計矣。

translations.literal: If the siege does not quickly yield surrender, assault cannot yet bring it down, covert routes cannot be used, gold and grain are not stored up, the realm is not of one house, and human sentiment cannot be foreseen—then one should further consider altering the plan.
translations.idiomatic: If the city will not fall soon, assault will not avail, no secret road is open, no hoard lies ready, the land is not one, and hearts cannot be read—then the plan itself must change.

sentences.zh: 變計之道，實資英斷，此之深要，難以紙宣，輒布言於席衛尉，特願垂采。

translations.literal: The way of altering plans truly depends on heroic resolve; its deeper essentials are hard to set down on paper; I venture to lay them before Minister Xi and especially hope he will lend his ear.
translations.idiomatic: To change course demands bold decision; what matters most cannot be written here—I lay it before Minister Xi and beg him to weigh it.

sentences.zh: 」高祖嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " Gaozu praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu approved and took the counsel to heart.

sentences.zh: 頃之，穎胄卒。

translations.literal: Before long Yinggou died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Yinggou died.

sentences.zh: 時高祖弟始興王憺留守襄陽，詳乃遣使迎憺，共參軍國。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu's brother the Prince of Shixing Dan was holding Xiangyang; Xiang sent envoys to welcome Dan to join in military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's brother the Prince of Shixing, Dan, was then holding Xiangyang; Xiang sent to bring him into counsel on army and state.

sentences.zh: 和帝加詳禁兵，出入殿省，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Emperor He added forbidden troops to Xiang, to enter and leave the palace offices; he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He offered him palace guards to pass in and out of the inner offices; Xiang refused outright.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant-in-ordinary and right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尋授使持節、撫軍將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was given Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Jingzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he received the staff as general who pacifies the army and inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 詳又固讓于憺。

translations.literal: Xiang again firmly yielded in favor of Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Again Xiang pressed his refusal in Dan's favor.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，徵爲侍中、車騎將軍，論功封寧都縣侯，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In Tianjian year 1 he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry; for merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningdu with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian he was recalled as attendant-in-ordinary and general of chariots and cavalry and, for merit, made marquis of Ningdu with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 詳累辭讓，至於懇切，乃更授右光祿大夫，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Xiang repeatedly declined, even to the point of earnest pleading; he was then instead made Right Grandee for Splendid Merit, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang declined again and again, until his plea was desperate; he was then given right grandee for splendid merit while keeping attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 給親信二十人，改封豊城縣公，邑如故。

translations.literal: He was given twenty trusted attendants; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Fengcheng, fief as before.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty trusted attendants were granted him, and his title was raised to duke of Fengcheng with the same fief.

sentences.zh: 二年，抗表致仕，詔解侍中，進特進。

translations.literal: In year 2 he memorialized to retire; an edict released him from Attendant-in-Ordinary and advanced him to Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he asked to leave office; the court removed him from attendant-in-ordinary and made him special advance.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷使持節、散騎常侍、車騎將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 3 he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Xiangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he went out with the staff as regular attendant, general of chariots and cavalry, and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 詳善吏事，在州四載，爲百姓所稱。

translations.literal: Xiang was skilled in administrative affairs; in the province four years, he was praised by the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang knew the work of office; through four years in the province the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 州城南臨水有峻峰，舊老相傳，云「刺史登此山輒被代。

translations.literal: South of the provincial city, facing the water, was a steep peak; old folk handed down the saying: "When an inspector climbs this mountain he is soon replaced."
translations.idiomatic: South of the city, above the river, stood a sharp peak; elders said, "Whichever inspector climbs this hill is soon replaced."

sentences.zh: 」因是歷政莫敢至。

translations.literal: For this reason successive administrations dared not go there.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason no governor had dared approach it.

sentences.zh: 詳於其地起臺榭，延僚屬，以表損挹之志。

translations.literal: Xiang built terraces and pavilions on the spot, invited his subordinates, and thereby showed his modest self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang raised halls and towers there, called his officers to him, and showed he did not fear the omen.

sentences.zh: 六年，徵爲侍中、右光祿大夫，給親信二十人，未至，授尚書左僕射、金紫光祿大夫，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In year 6 he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Grandee for Splendid Merit with twenty trusted attendants; before he arrived he was made Left Vice Director and Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Tassel, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recalled as attendant-in-ordinary and right grandee for splendid merit with twenty attendants; before he reached court he was named left vice director and grandee with the golden seal and purple tassel, still attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 道病卒，時年七十四，上爲素服舉哀，贈右光祿。

translations.literal: He died of illness on the road, aged seventy-four; the emperor wore plain mourning and raised lament; posthumously he was granted Right Grandee for Splendid Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the journey, at seventy-four; the emperor mourned in undyed dress and posthumously made him right grandee for splendid merit.

sentences.zh: 先是，荊府城局參軍起士瞻役萬人浚仗庫防火池，得金革帶鉤，隱起雕鏤甚精巧，篆文曰「錫爾金鉤，旣公且侯」。

translations.literal: Earlier, a city bureau aide of the Jing headquarters, Qi Shizhan, had conscripted ten thousand men to dig the armory's fire-prevention pool and found a belt hook of gold and leather, richly carved in relief; the inscription read: "We grant you a golden hook—already duke and marquis."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qi Shizhan, a city bureau aide in the Jing headquarters, had ten thousand men dig the armory's fire pool and unearthed a gold-and-leather belt hook, finely worked in relief, inscribed: "We grant you the golden hook—you are already duke and marquis."

sentences.zh: 士瞻，詳兄女婿也。

translations.literal: Shizhan was the son-in-law of Xiang's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhan had married the daughter of Xiang's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 女竊以與詳，詳喜佩之，期歲而貴矣。

translations.literal: The daughter secretly gave it to Xiang; Xiang delighted to wear it; within the year he had grown exalted.
translations.idiomatic: The girl stole it to Xiang; he wore it gladly, and within a year his rise had come.

sentences.zh: 蔡道恭，字懷儉，南陽冠軍人也。

translations.literal: Cai Daogong, styled Huaijian, was from Guanjun in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Daogong, styled Huaijian, came from Guanjun in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 父郡，宋益州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jun had been Song Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun had served as Song inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 道恭少寬厚有大量。

translations.literal: Daogong in youth was generous and broad in capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Daogong was open-handed and large-minded.

sentences.zh: 齊文帝爲雍州，召補主簿，仍除員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Qi Wendi was Prince of Yongzhou he was summoned to fill the post of chief clerk and was then made Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Wendi held Yongzhou he was called in as chief clerk and soon made supernumerary regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 後累有戰功，遷越騎校尉、後軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later, for repeated military merit, he was transferred to Colonel of the Swift Cavalry and Rear Army General.
translations.idiomatic: After further victories he rose to colonel of the swift cavalry and rear army general.

sentences.zh: 建武末，出爲輔國司馬、汝南令。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwu he went out as Major of the State-Supporting Army and Magistrate of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianwu he went out as state-supporting army major and magistrate of Runan.

sentences.zh: 齊南康王爲荊州，薦爲西中郎中兵參軍，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When the Qi Prince of Nankang held Jingzhou, Daogong was recommended as Army Aide of the Western Gentlemen and given the additional title General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Nankang took Jingzhou, Daogong was recommended as western palace army aide and made general who supports the state.

sentences.zh: 天監初，論功封漢壽縣伯，邑七百戶，進號平北將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, for merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hanshou with a fief of seven hundred households and advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian, for merit, he was made marquis of Hanshou with seven hundred households and promoted to general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 三年，魏圍司州，時城中衆不滿五千人，食裁支半歲，魏軍攻之，晝夜不息，道恭隨方抗禦，皆應手摧卻。

translations.literal: In year 3 Wei besieged Sizhou; at the time the city held fewer than five thousand men and food would barely last half a year; the Wei army attacked day and night without cease; Daogong met each thrust as it came and beat it back.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Wei laid siege to Sizhou; fewer than five thousand remained inside, with grain for barely half a year; Wei assaulted without pause, and Daogong turned back every blow.

sentences.zh: 魏乃作大車載土，四面俱前，欲以填壍，道恭輒於壍內列艨衝鬬艦以待之，魏人不得進。

translations.literal: Wei then built great wagons loaded with earth and advanced on all four sides, intending to fill the moat; Daogong lined the moat with tower ships and fighting vessels to receive them, and the Wei men could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei built great carts heaped with earth and pushed from every side to fill the ditch; Daogong set tower ships and battle craft in the moat to meet them, and they could not come on.

sentences.zh: 又潛作伏道以決壍水，道恭載土＜犭屯＞塞之。

translations.literal: They also secretly dug covered channels to drain the moat water; Daogong hauled earth in loads and tamped them shut.
translations.idiomatic: They dug hidden channels to draw off the moat; Daogong answered with basket after basket of earth rammed into the breach.

sentences.zh: 相持百餘日，前後斬獲不可勝計。

translations.literal: The standoff lasted more than a hundred days; those killed and captured before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a hundred days they held; the slain and taken mounted beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 魏大造梯沖，攻圍日急，道恭於城內作土山，厚二十餘丈；

translations.literal: Wei built great scaling ladders and battering engines, and the siege grew daily more urgent; Daogong raised an earthen mountain inside the city more than twenty zhang high;
translations.idiomatic: Wei raised siege towers and rams, and the press of attack tightened; inside the walls Daogong piled an earthen hill twenty zhang and more;

sentences.zh: 多作大槊，長二丈五尺，施長刃，使壯士刺魏人登城者。

translations.literal: he made many long spears, two zhang five feet in length, fitted with long blades, and set strong men to stab the Wei soldiers climbing the walls.
translations.idiomatic: he forged long pikes two zhang five feet long with heavy blades and set his stoutest men to spear the Wei climbers on the walls.

sentences.zh: 魏軍甚憚之，將退。

translations.literal: The Wei army greatly feared this and was about to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Wei grew afraid of these weapons and prepared to pull back.

sentences.zh: 會道恭疾篤，乃呼兄子僧勰、從弟靈恩及諸將帥謂曰：「吾受國厚恩，不能破滅寇賊，今所苦轉篤，勢不支久，汝等當以死固節，無令吾沒有遺恨。

translations.literal: It happened that Daogong's illness grew grave; he called his elder brother's son Sengyi, his younger cousin Ling'en, and the generals and said: "I have received the state's deep grace and could not destroy the bandit horde; my suffering now grows worse and I cannot hold out much longer—you must hold fast unto death and not let me die with regret."
translations.idiomatic: Then Daogong's sickness turned mortal; he summoned his nephew Sengyi, his cousin Ling'en, and the commanders and said, "The state loaded me with favor, yet I could not break the enemy; my pain deepens and the wall cannot stand long—you must die where you stand and leave me no shame in the grave."

sentences.zh: 」又令取所持節謂僧勰曰：「稟命出疆，憑此而已；

translations.literal: He also ordered his staff of office brought and told Sengyi: "To bear the mandate beyond the border—on this alone I relied;
translations.idiomatic: He had his credential staff brought and told Sengyi, "I crossed the frontier on this charge alone;

sentences.zh: 卽不得奉以還朝，方欲攜之同逝，可與棺柩相隨。

translations.literal: since I cannot bear it back to court, I mean to carry it with me in death; let it follow the coffin."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot return it to the throne—then let it go into the earth with me beside the coffin."

sentences.zh: 」衆皆流涕。

translations.literal: All wept.
translations.idiomatic: Every man wept.

sentences.zh: 其年五月卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of that year.

sentences.zh: 魏知道恭死，攻之轉急。

translations.literal: When Wei learned Daogong was dead, their attacks grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Daogong was gone, Wei pressed the assault all the harder.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷遣郢州刺史曹景宗率衆赴援，景宗到鑿峴，頓兵不前。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had sent Yingzhou Inspector Cao Jingzong with an army to relieve the city; Jingzong reached Zao Gorge and halted his troops without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already sent Cao Jingzong of Yingzhou with a relief host; Jingzong came to Zao Gorge and camped without moving.

sentences.zh: 至八月，城內糧盡，乃陷。

translations.literal: By the eighth month grain inside the city was exhausted, and it fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the city's grain ran out, and Sizhou fell.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「持節、都督司州諸軍事、平北將軍、司州刺史、漢壽縣開國伯道恭，器幹詳審，才志通烈。

translations.literal: Edict: "Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Sizhou, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Sizhou, and Founding Marquis of Hanshou Daogong—his capacity and conduct are thorough and careful, his talent and will penetrating and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Sizhou, general who pacifies the north, inspector of Sizhou, and founding marquis of Hanshou, Cai Daogong—his mind was careful, his talent fierce and clear.

sentences.zh: 王業肇構，致力陝西。

translations.literal: From the first founding of the royal enterprise he devoted his strength in the western marches.
translations.idiomatic: From the first days of the founding he gave his strength to the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 受任邊垂，效彰所蒞。

translations.literal: Receiving appointment on the border, his achievements shone in every post he held.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier his service shone wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 寇賊憑陵，竭誠守禦，奇謀間出，捷書日至。

translations.literal: When bandits pressed upon us, he defended with utter loyalty; stratagems issued one after another, and reports of victory came day by day.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy closed in he held with full loyalty, scheming without rest and sending victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 不幸抱疾，奄至殞喪，遺略所固，得移氣朔。

translations.literal: Alas that, seized by illness, he suddenly fell—yet the defense he left behind held firm and shifted the enemy's momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly illness took him—but the ramparts he left stood, and even in death he turned the season against the foe.

sentences.zh: 自非徇國忘已，忠果並至，何能身沒守存，窮而後屈。

translations.literal: Had he not forgotten himself for the state and joined loyalty with steadfast fruit, how could he die yet leave the defense standing, exhausted yet unbent at the last?
translations.idiomatic: Only one who gives himself to the realm and binds loyalty to resolve could die and still keep the city, spent yet unbroken.

sentences.zh: 言念傷悼，特兼常懷，追榮加等。

translations.literal: When I think on this, grief wounds my breast; let special honors be added beyond the usual measure.
translations.idiomatic: My heart grieves at the thought; let his reward exceed the common rule.

sentences.zh: 抑有恒數。

translations.literal: This too has its constant precedent.
translations.idiomatic: So the rites also command.

sentences.zh: 可贈鎮西將軍，使持節、都督、刺史、伯如故，幷尋購喪櫬，隨宜資給。

translations.literal: Let him be posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West; Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief, Inspector, and Marquis as before; let his coffin be sought out and provisions made as fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made general who pacifies the west, with staff, command, inspectorship, and marquisate unchanged; seek out his coffin and grant what the occasion requires.

sentences.zh: 」八年，魏許還道恭喪，其家以女樂易之，葬襄陽。

translations.literal: " In year 8 Wei agreed to return Daogong's remains; his family exchanged female musicians for them, and he was buried at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth year Wei agreed to send back his body; the family traded court musicians for it, and he was buried at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 子澹嗣，卒於河東太守。

translations.literal: His son Dan succeeded; he died while Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dan inherited the title and died as administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 孫固早卒，國除。

translations.literal: Grandson Gu died young, and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Gu died early and the marquisate was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 楊公則，字君翼，天水西縣人也。

translations.literal: Yang Gongze, styled Junyi, was from Xi county in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze, styled Junyi, came from Xi county in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父仲懷，宋泰始初爲豫州刺史殷琰將。

translations.literal: His father Zhonghuai in the first year of Song Taishi was a general under Yin Yan, Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhonghuai, in the first year of Song Taishi, served as a general under Yin Yan, inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 琰叛，輔國將軍劉勔討琰，仲懷力戰，死於橫塘。

translations.literal: When Yan rebelled, Support-the-State General Liu Xu attacked him; Zhonghuai fought fiercely and died at Hengtang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan rose in rebellion, Liu Xu, general who supports the state, marched against him; Zhonghuai fought hard and fell at Hengtang.

sentences.zh: 公則隨父在軍，年未弱冠，冒陣抱尸號哭，氣絕良久，勔命還仲懷首。

translations.literal: Gongze had followed his father in the army; though not yet of age, he dashed into the ranks, embraced the corpse, and wailed until breath left him for a long while; Xu ordered Zhonghuai's head returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze was with the army though still a boy; he broke into the line, caught up his father's body, and cried until he fainted; Xu had the head sent back.

sentences.zh: 公則殮畢，徒步負喪歸鄉里，由此著名。

translations.literal: When the burial was done, Gongze walked on foot, carrying the coffin home to his native place, and thereby became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites he bore the coffin home on foot and won fame for it.

sentences.zh: 歷官員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed through the offices to Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through office to supernumerary regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史范柏年板爲宋熙太守、領白馬戍主。

translations.literal: Liangzhou Inspector Fan Bonian appointed him Administrator of Songxi and commandant of the White Horse garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bonian, inspector of Liangzhou, made him administrator of Songxi and commandant of White Horse garrison.

sentences.zh: 氐賊李烏奴作亂，攻白馬，公則固守經時，矢盡糧竭，陷于寇，抗聲罵賊。

translations.literal: The Di bandit Li Wunu rebelled and attacked White Horse; Gongze held firm for a long time until arrows and grain were spent, then fell to the bandits; he shouted curses at them in a loud voice.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Li Wunu rose and struck White Horse; Gongze held until shafts and grain were gone, then was taken; he cursed the enemy without lowering his voice.

sentences.zh: 烏奴壯之，更厚待焉，要與同事。

translations.literal: Wunu admired his spirit and treated him all the more generously, inviting him to join in their enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Wunu honored his courage and treated him well, asking him to serve alongside them.

sentences.zh: 公則偽許而圖之，謀泄，單馬逃歸。

translations.literal: Gongze pretended to agree while plotting against them; when the plot leaked, he fled home on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze feigned consent and plotted their ruin; when the plot was discovered he escaped alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史王玄邈以事表聞，齊高帝下詔褒美。

translations.literal: Liangzhou Inspector Wang Xuanmiao reported the matter in a memorial; Qi Gaodi issued an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmiao, inspector of Liangzhou, memorialized the court; Qi Gaodi issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 除晉壽太守，在任清潔自守。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Jinshou and in his post was pure, holding himself with integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Jinshou and governed with clean hands.

sentences.zh: 永明中，爲鎮北長流參軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he was Army Aide on the Northern Garrison staff of the General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongming era he served as army aide on the northern garrison staff under the general who guards the north.

sentences.zh: 遷扶風太守，母憂去官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administrator of Fufeng and left office on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He became administrator of Fufeng, then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史陳顯達起爲寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Inspector Chen Xianda raised him as General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou inspector Chen Xianda raised him as General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 復領太守。

translations.literal: He again held the post of administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He again held the post of administrator.

sentences.zh: 頃之，荊州刺史巴東王子響構亂，公則率師進討。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Badong, Jingzhou inspector, plotted rebellion; Gongze led troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the Prince of Badong, as Jingzhou inspector, raised rebellion; Gongze marched against him.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷武寧太守。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was transferred to administrator of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, he was made administrator of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 在郡七年，資無擔石，百姓便之。

translations.literal: Seven years in the commandery, his household not a dan and stone to its name; the common people found his rule a blessing.
translations.idiomatic: For seven years in the commandery he owned scarcely a bushel of grain, yet the people flourished under him.

sentences.zh: 入爲前軍將軍。

translations.literal: He entered office as General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 南康王爲荊州，復爲西中郎中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nankang held Jingzhou, he again became western middle army central military aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Nankang took Jingzhou, he again served as western middle army central military aide.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍蕭穎胄協同義舉，以公則爲輔國將軍、領西中郎諮議參軍，中兵如故，率衆東下。

translations.literal: Commandant of Guards Xiao Yingmao joined the righteous rising and made Gongze General Who Supports the State, concurrent western middle army consultant aide, central army duties unchanged, and led his forces east.
translations.idiomatic: When Commandant of Guards Xiao Yingmao joined the righteous rising, Gongze was made General Who Supports the State and concurrent western middle army consultant aide, kept his central army post, and led his men east.

sentences.zh: 時湘州行事張寶積發兵自守，未知所附，公則軍及巴陵，仍回師南討。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Baoji, acting for Xiangzhou, had raised troops to hold himself and did not know whom to follow; Gongze's army reached Baling and turned south to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baoji, acting for Xiangzhou, had mobilized to hold his ground and wavered between sides; when Gongze reached Baling he swung south to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 軍次白沙，寶積懼，釋甲以俟焉。

translations.literal: The army halted at Baisha; Baoji grew afraid, laid down arms, and waited.
translations.idiomatic: The army stopped at Baisha; Baoji, afraid, disarmed and waited.

sentences.zh: 公則到，撫納之，湘境遂定。

translations.literal: When Gongze arrived he comforted and accepted him, and Xiang territory was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze arrived, reassured him, and took him in; Xiang was pacified.

sentences.zh: 和帝卽位，授持節、都督湘州諸軍事、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor He ascended, Gongze was granted Bearer of the Staff, superintendent of all military affairs of Xiangzhou, and inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He took the throne, Gongze received the staff, command of Xiangzhou forces, and the inspectorship of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖勒衆軍次於沔口，魯山城主孫樂祖、郢州刺史張沖各據城未下，公則率湘府之衆會于夏口。

translations.literal: Gaozu halted the massed armies at Hankou; Sun Lezu, lord of Lushan city, and Yingzhou Inspector Zhang Chong each held a city not yet taken; Gongze led the Xiang office troops to join at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu camped the main armies at Hankou while Sun Lezu held Lushan and Zhang Chong held Ying; Gongze brought the Xiang forces to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 時荊州諸軍受公則節度，雖蕭穎達宗室之貴亦隸焉。

translations.literal: At the time all Jingzhou armies were under Gongze's command; even Xiao Yingda of the imperial clan's eminence was subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Every army in Jingzhou now answered to Gongze—even Xiao Yingda of the imperial house marched under his orders.

sentences.zh: 累進征虜將軍、左衛將軍，持節、刺史如故。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General Who Captures the Barbarians and Left Guard General; Bearer of the Staff and inspector remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Captures the Barbarians and Left Guard General, keeping the staff and the inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 郢城平，高祖命衆軍卽日俱下，公則受命先驅，徑掩柴桑。

translations.literal: When Ying city fell, Gaozu ordered every army to march down that same day; Gongze received orders as vanguard and struck straight at Chaisang.
translations.idiomatic: Ying fell; Gaozu ordered a general advance that day; Gongze went first and seized Chaisang.

sentences.zh: 江州旣定，連旌東下，直造京邑。

translations.literal: When Jiangzhou was settled, linked banners moved east and went straight to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou secured, the banners turned east and bore straight on the capital.

sentences.zh: 公則號令嚴明，秋毫不犯，所在莫不賴焉。

translations.literal: Gongze's orders were strict and clear; not a hair was harmed; wherever he passed, people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze's discipline was iron; nothing was taken; wherever his men went, people trusted them.

sentences.zh: 大軍至新林，公則自越城移屯領軍府壘北樓，與南掖門相對，嘗登樓望戰。

translations.literal: When the great army reached Xinlin, Gongze moved from Yue city to camp at the north tower of the Commandant of Guards headquarters rampart, opposite the South Yeb Gate, and once climbed the tower to watch the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinlin, Gongze shifted from Yue city to the north tower of the commandant's rampart, facing the South Yeb Gate, and watched the battle from above.

sentences.zh: 城中遙見麾蓋，縱神鋒弩射之，矢貫胡床，左右皆失色。

translations.literal: In the city men saw his banners and canopy from afar and let fly divine-edge crossbows; an arrow pierced his folding chair, and those at his side all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: From the walls they saw his canopy and shot with divine-edge crossbows; a bolt drove through his camp chair, and his attendants blanched.

sentences.zh: 公則曰：「幾中吾腳。

translations.literal: Gongze said: "Nearly hit my foot.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze said, "That almost took my foot.

sentences.zh: 」談笑如初。

translations.literal: " He talked and laughed as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he joked as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 東昏夜選勇士攻公則柵，軍中驚擾，公則堅臥不起，徐命擊之，東昏軍乃退。

translations.literal: Dong Hun at night chose brave men to attack Gongze's palisade; the army was alarmed and stirred, but Gongze lay firm and would not rise, slowly ordered a counterattack, and Dong Hun's troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hun sent picked warriors by night against Gongze's camp; the lines panicked, but Gongze stayed in bed, gave the order to strike, and the enemy fell back.

sentences.zh: 公則所領多湘溪人，性怯懦，城內輕之，以爲易與，每出蕩，輒先犯公則壘。

translations.literal: Gongze's troops were mostly men of the Xiang streams, by nature timid; inside the city they were despised as easy prey, and whenever raiders went out they always struck Gongze's camp first.
translations.idiomatic: His men were mostly Xiang river folk, thought soft; the defenders mocked them and made Gongze's camp their first target on every sortie.

sentences.zh: 公則獎厲軍士，剋獲更多。

translations.literal: Gongze encouraged his soldiers, and they took more captives and booty.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze roused his troops, and they brought back richer spoils each time.

sentences.zh: 及平，城內出者或被剝奪，公則親率麾下，列陣東掖門，衛送公卿士庶，故出者多由公則營焉。

translations.literal: When the city was pacified, those who came out were sometimes stripped and robbed; Gongze personally led his men and formed ranks at the East Yeb Gate to guard and escort nobles and commoners, so most who left passed through Gongze's camp.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall, looters preyed on those leaving the city; Gongze lined his men at the East Yeb Gate and escorted officials and people safely out, and most exits ran through his camp.

sentences.zh: 進號左將軍，持節、刺史如故，還鎮南蕃。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Left General; Bearer of the Staff and inspector remained as before, and he returned to garrison the southern marches.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left General, kept staff and inspectorship, and returned to hold the south.

sentences.zh: 初，公則東下，湘部諸郡多未賓從，及公則還州，然後諸屯聚並散。

translations.literal: When Gongze had first marched east, many commanderies of the Xiang region had not yet submitted; when Gongze returned to the province, then all fortified clusters dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: On his first march east many Xiang commanderies had held back; only when he came back did the hill forts melt away.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，進號平南將軍，封寧都縣侯，邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: In Tianjian year 1 he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningdu district with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 1 he became General Who Pacifies the South and Marquis of Ningdu with fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 湘州寇亂累年，民多流散，公則輕刑薄斂，頃之，戶口充復。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou had suffered banditry for years and the people had scattered; Gongze lightened punishments and levies, and before long households filled and were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Years of raiding had emptied Xiangzhou; Gongze eased law and tax, and soon the registers swelled again.

sentences.zh: 爲政雖無威嚴，然保己廉慎，爲吏民所悅。

translations.literal: In governance he lacked awe-inspiring sternness, yet he kept himself in integrity and caution, and officials and commoners loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled without harsh display, but he was honest and careful, and officials and people adored him.

sentences.zh: 湘俗單家以賂求州職，公則至，悉斷之，所辟引皆州郡著姓，高祖班下諸州以爲法。

translations.literal: In Xiang custom lone families used bribes to win provincial posts; when Gongze arrived he cut it all off; those he recruited were all prominent surnames of province and commandery, and Gaozu circulated his example to every province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang families had bought office with gifts; Gongze ended that, appointed only notable local houses, and Gaozu made every province follow his model.

sentences.zh: 四年，徵中護軍。

translations.literal: In year 4 he was summoned to be Central Army Protector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was called to the capital as Central Army Protector.

sentences.zh: 代至，乘二舸便發，贐送一無所取。

translations.literal: When his successor arrived he boarded two light boats and set out at once, taking none of the farewell gifts.
translations.idiomatic: His replacement came; he took two light boats and left that day, refusing every parting gift.

sentences.zh: 仍遷衛尉卿，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Court Commandant with the additional title Palace Attendant Who Remains at Ease.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Court Commandant and Palace Attendant Who Remains at Ease.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷始議北伐，以公則威名素著，至京師，詔假節先屯洛口。

translations.literal: The court had begun to discuss a northern expedition; because Gongze's repute was long established, on reaching the capital an edict granted him temporary staff to encamp first at Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: As the court debated a northern campaign, Gongze's fame brought him to the capital with orders to take the staff and hold Luokou ahead of the army.

sentences.zh: 公則受命遘疾，謂親人曰：「昔廉頗、馬援以年老見遺，猶自力請用。

translations.literal: On receiving his orders Gongze fell ill and told those close to him: "In old days Lian Po and Ma Yuan, though set aside for age, still strove to ask for employment.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze took the commission but fell ill and told his kin, "Long ago Lian Po and Ma Yuan were cast off as old men, yet they still begged to serve.

sentences.zh: 今國家不以吾朽懦，任以前驅，方於古人，見知重矣。

translations.literal: Now the state does not regard my decayed weakness and appoints me vanguard—compared with the ancients, the trust is weighty indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The state does not despise my frailty but puts me in the van—that is heavier honor than they knew.

sentences.zh: 雖臨途疾苦，豈可僶俛辭事。

translations.literal: Though illness afflicts me on the road, how can I bow my head and decline the charge?
translations.idiomatic: I am sick on the march, but how can I cringe away from the task?

sentences.zh: 馬革還葬，此吾志也。

translations.literal: Burial wrapped in horse hide—this is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: To come home in horse leather—that is what I want.

sentences.zh: 」遂強起登舟。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he forced himself up and boarded ship.
translations.idiomatic: " He dragged himself aboard.

sentences.zh: 至洛口，壽春士女歸降者數千戶。

translations.literal: Reaching Luokou, gentlemen and women of Shouchun who submitted numbered several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At Luokou several thousand households of Shouchun came over to him.

sentences.zh: 魏豫州刺史薛恭度遣長史石榮前鋒接戰，卽斬石榮，逐北至壽春，去城數十里乃反。

translations.literal: Wei Yuzhou Inspector Xue Gongdu sent Chief Clerk Shi Rong as vanguard to meet battle; Gongze at once beheaded Shi Rong, pursued north to Shouchun, and turned back only when several tens of li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Yuzhou inspector Xue Gongdu sent his chief clerk Shi Rong to fight; Gongze killed him at once, chased to Shouchun, and withdrew ten-odd li from the walls.

sentences.zh: 疾卒于師，時年六十一。

translations.literal: He died of illness in the army, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Illness took him in camp at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 高祖深痛惜之，卽日舉哀，贈車騎將軍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Gaozu grieved deeply, held mourning that same day, and posthumously made him General of Chariots and Cavalry with one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu mourned him the same day, posthumously made him General of Chariots and Cavalry, and granted martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 諡曰烈。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Lie.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Lie, "Fierce."

sentences.zh: 公則爲人敦厚慈愛，居家篤睦，視兄子過於其子，家財悉委焉。

translations.literal: Gongze was by nature thick in kindness and love; at home he was devoted and harmonious, regarded his brother's sons more than his own, and entrusted all family wealth to them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongze was gentle and warm at home, favored his brother's sons over his own, and gave them the whole household fortune.

sentences.zh: 性好學，雖居軍旅，手不輟卷，士大夫以此稱之。

translations.literal: He loved learning; though in the army his hand never left the scroll, and scholar-officials praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books; even in camp he read without pause, and the gentry spoke of it with respect.

sentences.zh: 子膘嗣，有罪國除。

translations.literal: His son Biao succeeded; he committed a crime and the fief was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Biao inherited, then forfeited the fief for a crime.

sentences.zh: 高祖以公則勳臣，特詔聽庶長子朓嗣。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because Gongze was a meritorious minister, issued a special edict allowing the eldest son by a concubine, Tuan, to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, honoring Gongze's service, specially allowed his eldest son by a concubine, Tuan, to inherit.

sentences.zh: 朓固讓，歷年乃受。

translations.literal: Tuan firmly declined; only after years did he accept.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan refused for years before he would take the title.

sentences.zh: 鄧元起，字仲居，南郡當陽人也。

translations.literal: Deng Yuanqi, styled Zhongju, was a native of Dangyang in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuanqi, styled Zhongju, came from Dangyang in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有膽幹，膂力過人。

translations.literal: In youth he had courage and ability; his physical strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and strong beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 性任俠，好賑施，鄉里年少多附之。

translations.literal: By nature chivalrous, he loved giving relief; many young men of the village attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was a rover who gave freely, and the young men of the countryside followed him.

sentences.zh: 起家州辟議曹從事史，轉奉朝請。

translations.literal: He began his career with a provincial summons as aide in the discussion affairs bureau and was transferred to Court Gentleman for the Court.
translations.idiomatic: The province first summoned him as discussion-affairs aide; he later became a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史蕭緬板爲槐里令。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Inspector Xiao Mian commissioned him magistrate of Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou inspector Xiao Mian appointed him magistrate of Huaili.

sentences.zh: 遷弘農太守、平西軍事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administrator of Hongnong and western pacification military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became administrator of Hongnong and held western pacification military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時西陽馬榮率衆緣江寇抄，商旅斷絕，刺史蕭遙欣使元起率衆討平之。
