translations.literal: At the time Ma Rong of Xiyang led masses along the river to raid and plunder, cutting off merchants and travelers; Inspector Xiao Yaoxin sent Yuanqi to lead troops and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong of Xiyang was raiding along the river and choking trade; inspector Xiao Yaoxin sent Yuanqi to crush him.

sentences.zh: 遷武寧太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administrator of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 永元末，魏軍逼義陽，元起自郡援焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan the Wei army pressed Yiyang; Yuanqi marched from his commandery to its relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Yongyuan Wei pressed Yiyang; Yuanqi came from his commandery to help.

sentences.zh: 蠻帥田孔明附于魏，自號郢州刺史，寇掠三關，規襲夏口，元起率銳卒攻之，旬月之間，頻陷六城，斬獲萬計，餘黨悉皆散走。

translations.literal: The Man chief Tian Kongming had attached himself to Wei, styled himself Yingzhou inspector, raided the Three Passes, and plotted to strike Xiakou; Yuanqi led elite troops against him and within a month repeatedly took six cities, beheaded and captured by the tens of thousands, and the remnant factions all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Man leader Tian Kongming joined Wei, called himself Yingzhou inspector, and raided the Three Passes toward Xiakou; Yuanqi struck with picked men, took six towns in a month, killed and captured by the ten thousands, and broke the rest.

sentences.zh: 仍戍三關。

translations.literal: He thereupon garrisoned the Three Passes.
translations.idiomatic: He then held the Three Passes.

sentences.zh: 郢州刺史張沖督河北軍事，元起累與沖書，求旋軍。

translations.literal: Yingzhou Inspector Zhang Chong supervised military affairs north of the river; Yuanqi repeatedly wrote Chong asking to withdraw his army.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou inspector Zhang Chong commanded north of the river; Yuanqi wrote again and again asking leave to return.

sentences.zh: 沖報書曰：「足下在彼，吾在此，表裏之勢，所謂金城湯池；

translations.literal: Chong replied in a letter: "You there and I here—an inside-outside position, what they call a metal city and boiling pool;
translations.idiomatic: Chong answered, "You hold one gate and I the other—that is the golden rampart and boiling moat.

sentences.zh: 一旦舍去，則荊棘生焉。

translations.literal: once you abandon it, brambles will grow."
translations.idiomatic: Leave it, and thorns spring up at once."

sentences.zh: 」乃表元起爲平南中兵參軍事。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized Yuanqi as southern pacification central army military aide.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized Yuanqi as southern pacification central army military aide.

sentences.zh: 自是每戰必捷，勇冠當時，敢死之士樂爲用命者萬有餘人。

translations.literal: From this time every battle was a victory; his courage crowned the age, and men willing to die for him numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After that he won every fight; no one matched his daring, and more than ten thousand men would die for him.

sentences.zh: 義師起，蕭穎胄與書招之。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Xiao Yingmao summoned him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous cause rose, Xiao Yingmao called him by letter.

sentences.zh: 張沖待元起素厚，衆皆懼沖；

translations.literal: Zhang Chong had always treated Yuanqi generously, and the masses all feared Chong;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong had long favored Yuanqi, and the troops feared offending him;

sentences.zh: 及書至，元起部曲多勸其還郢。

translations.literal: when the letter arrived, many of Yuanqi's followers urged him to return to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: when the summons came, many of his officers urged him back to Ying.

sentences.zh: 元起大言於衆曰：「朝廷暴虐，誅戮宰臣，羣小用命，衣冠道盡。

translations.literal: Yuanqi spoke grandly to the masses: "The court is violent and cruel, executing chief ministers; petty men wield commands, and the way of rites and caps is utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi addressed the host: "The throne is savage, butchers its ministers, and lets lackeys rule—the rites are dead.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍二州同舉大事，何患不剋。

translations.literal: Jing and Yong together raise a great affair—what worry is there of not conquering?
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Yong rise together—how can we fail?

sentences.zh: 且我老母在西，豈容背本。

translations.literal: Moreover my old mother is in the west—how could I turn my back on my roots?
translations.idiomatic: My mother is still in the west—I cannot betray my home.

sentences.zh: 若事不成，政受戮昏朝，倖免不孝之罪。

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, let me simply receive execution from this benighted court and luckily escape the crime of unfiliality."
translations.idiomatic: If we lose, let the dark court kill me and spare me the shame of a bad son."

sentences.zh: 」卽日治嚴上道。

translations.literal: That same day he prepared baggage and took the road.
translations.idiomatic: That day he packed and marched.

sentences.zh: 至江陵，爲西中郎中兵參軍，加冠軍將軍，率衆與高祖會于夏口。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangling, he was made western middle army central military aide with the additional title Champion General, led his masses, and joined Gaozu at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling he became western middle army central military aide and Champion General, then led his men to Gaozu at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 高祖命王茂、曹景宗及元起等圍城，結壘九里，張沖屢戰，輒大敗，乃嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, and Yuanqi and the rest to besiege the city, linking ramparts for nine li; Zhang Chong fought repeatedly and was always heavily defeated, then closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu set Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, and Yuanqi to siege Ying with ramparts nine li long; Zhang Chong fought and lost again and again, then shut the gates and endured.

sentences.zh: 初，義師之起，益州刺史劉季連持兩端；

translations.literal: When the righteous army first rose, Yizhou Inspector Liu Jilian had held both ends;
translations.idiomatic: At first Yizhou inspector Liu Jilian had sat on the fence;

sentences.zh: 及聞元起將至，遂發兵拒守。

translations.literal: when he heard Yuanqi was coming, he sent troops to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: but when he heard Yuanqi was coming he armed the passes and resisted.

sentences.zh: 語在《季連傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Liu Jilian.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller account is in Liu Jilian's biography.

sentences.zh: 元起至巴西，巴西太守硃士略開門以待。

translations.literal: When Yuanqi reached Baxi, Baxi Administrator Zhu Shilue opened the gates to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi reached Baxi, and administrator Zhu Shilue opened the city to him.

sentences.zh: 先時蜀人多逃亡，至是出投元起，皆稱起義應朝廷，師人新故三萬餘。

translations.literal: Earlier many people of Shu had fled; now they came out to join Yuanqi, all calling it a righteous rising in answer to the court; new and old in the army numbered more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu refugees who had hidden now flocked to him as men answering the throne; his army, old and new, passed thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 元起在道久，軍糧乏絕。

translations.literal: Yuanqi had been long on the road and army grain was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi had marched so long that the granaries were empty.

sentences.zh: 或說之曰：「蜀土政慢，民多詐疾，若儉巴西一郡籍注，困而罰之，所獲必厚。

translations.literal: Someone advised him: "Shu governance is slack and the people often feign illness; if you investigate the register of Baxi commandery alone, distress them and punish them, the harvest will surely be rich."
translations.idiomatic: An adviser said, "Shu is slack and the people lie about sickness; audit one commandery, Baxi, squeeze and fine them, and you will fill the stores."

sentences.zh: 」元起然之。

translations.literal: Yuanqi approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi agreed.

sentences.zh: 涪令李膺諫曰：「使君前有嚴敵，後無繼援，山民始附，於我觀德，若糾以刻薄，民必不堪，衆心一離，雖悔無及，何必起疾，可以濟師。

translations.literal: Fuling Magistrate Li Ying remonstrated: "My lord has a fierce enemy ahead and no relief behind; the hill people have just attached themselves and are watching our virtue—if you investigate them with harshness the people cannot bear it, and once hearts divide, though you regret it nothing can be done. Why must you raise illness when you can thereby supply the army?
translations.idiomatic: Fuling magistrate Li Ying warned him, "You face a hard enemy ahead with no help behind; the hill folk have only just joined and are watching how you rule. Harsh levies will break them, and once they turn away you cannot win them back. Why invite trouble when you can feed the army another way?

sentences.zh: 膺請出圖之，不患資糧不足也。

translations.literal: Let Ying go out and devise a plan; there is no need to fear insufficient provisions."
translations.idiomatic: Let me try, and you will not lack grain."

sentences.zh: 」元起曰：「善，一以委卿。

translations.literal: Yuanqi said: "Good—I entrust it all to you."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi said, "Good—do as you will."

sentences.zh: 」膺退，率富民上軍資米，俄得三萬斛。

translations.literal: Ying withdrew, led wealthy households to submit army grain, and soon obtained thirty thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying left, rallied the rich to bring rice, and within days raised thirty thousand hu.

sentences.zh: 元起先遣將王元宗等，破季連將李奉伯於新巴，齊晚盛於赤水，衆進屯西平。

translations.literal: Yuanqi had earlier sent the generals Wang Yuanzong and the rest to defeat Jilian's general Li Fengbo at Xinba and Qi Wansheng at Chishui; the masses advanced and encamped at Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi had already sent Wang Yuanzong and others to beat Liu Jilian's Li Fengbo at Xinba and Qi Wansheng at Chishui, then pushed the host to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 季連始嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Jilian then closed the city and held in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jilian finally shut Chengdu and dug in.

sentences.zh: 晚盛又破元起將魯方達於斛石，士卒死者千餘人，師衆咸懼，元起乃自率兵稍進至蔣橋，去成都二十里，留輜重於郫。

translations.literal: Wansheng again defeated Yuanqi's general Lu Fangda at Hushi; more than a thousand soldiers died; the army was afraid; Yuanqi then personally led troops and gradually advanced to Jiangqiao, twenty li from Chengdu, leaving baggage at Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wansheng crushed Lu Fangda at Hushi and killed more than a thousand; the army shook; Yuanqi led the van himself to Jiangqiao, twenty li from Chengdu, and left the baggage at Pi.

sentences.zh: 季連復遣奉伯、晚盛二千人，間道襲郫，陷之，軍備盡沒。

translations.literal: Jilian again sent Fengbo and Wansheng with two thousand men by a hidden path to raid Pi, took it, and all military stores were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Jilian sent Fengbo and Wansheng with two thousand men by a bypath, seized Pi, and burned Yuanqi's stores.

sentences.zh: 元起遣魯方達之衆救之，敗而反，遂不能剋。

translations.literal: Yuanqi sent Lu Fangda's troops to the rescue; they were defeated and returned, and he could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi sent Lu Fangda to retake it; he was beaten back and could not break through.

sentences.zh: 元起捨郫，逕圍州城，柵其三面而塹焉。

translations.literal: Yuanqi abandoned Pi, went straight to besiege the provincial city, palisaded three sides, and dug moats.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi left Pi, ringed the provincial capital on three sides, and dug trenches.

sentences.zh: 元起出巡視圍柵，季連使精勇掩之，將至麾下，元起下輿持楯叱之，衆辟易不敢進。

translations.literal: Yuanqi went out to inspect the siege palisades; Jilian sent elite troops to ambush him; when they were about to reach his presence, Yuanqi descended from his carriage, held a shield, and shouted; the masses scattered and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi walked the lines; Jilian sent killers to rush him; as they closed in he stepped down, raised his shield, and roared them off.

sentences.zh: 時益部兵亂日久，民廢耕農，內外苦饑，人多相食，道路斷絕，季連計窮。

translations.literal: Military chaos in Yizhou had lasted long; the people abandoned farming; inside and outside suffered bitter hunger; many ate one another; roads were cut off; Jilian's plans were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: War had raged so long in Yizhou that fields lay waste, hunger ruled inside and out, men fed on men, and the roads were dead; Jilian was at his end.

sentences.zh: 會明年，高祖使赦季連罪，許之降。

translations.literal: The next year Gaozu sent orders pardoning Jilian's crimes and permitting his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Gaozu pardoned Jilian and promised to accept his surrender.

sentences.zh: 季連卽日開城納元起，元起送季連于京師。

translations.literal: Jilian that same day opened the city and admitted Yuanqi; Yuanqi sent Jilian to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jilian opened the gates that day; Yuanqi took the city and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 城開，郫乃降。

translations.literal: When the city opened, Pi then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the city opened, Pi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 斬奉伯、晚盛。

translations.literal: He beheaded Fengbo and Wansheng.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Fengbo and Wansheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖論平蜀勳，復元起號平西將軍，增封八百戶，幷前二千戶。

translations.literal: Gaozu assessed merit for pacifying Shu, restored Yuanqi's title General Who Pacifies the West, added eight hundred households to his fief, and with the previous grant made two thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu weighed merit for pacifying Shu, restored Yuanqi as General Who Pacifies the West, added eight hundred households to his fief, and with the earlier grant brought the total to two thousand.

sentences.zh: 元起以鄉人庾黔婁爲錄事參軍，又得荊州刺史蕭遙欣故客蔣光濟，並厚待之，任以州事。

translations.literal: Yuanqi appointed his fellow townsman Yu Qianlou as Recording Secretary aide, and also obtained Jingzhou Inspector Xiao Yaoxin's former retainer Jiang Guangji; he treated both generously and entrusted them with provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi made his townsman Yu Qianlou recording secretary aide and took on Xiao Yaoxin's former guest Jiang Guangji; both were richly favored and given charge of the province.

sentences.zh: 黔婁甚清潔，光濟多計謀，並勸爲善政。

translations.literal: Qianlou was very upright and clean; Guangji was full of stratagems; both urged good government.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlou was scrupulously honest, Guangji resourceful in counsel, and both pressed for sound rule.

sentences.zh: 元起之剋季連也，城內財寶無所私，勤恤民事，口不論財色。

translations.literal: When Yuanqi overcame Jilian, he took none of the city's treasures for himself, diligently cared for the people's affairs, and never spoke of wealth or women.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanqi defeated Jilian he kept none of the city's wealth, worked hard for the people, and never spoke of money or women.

sentences.zh: 性本能飲酒，至一斛不亂，及是絕之。

translations.literal: By nature he could drink well—to a hu without losing control—and now he gave it up entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He could naturally drink a hu without disorder, but from then on he abstained completely.

sentences.zh: 蜀土翕然稱之。

translations.literal: Shu lands unanimously praised him.
translations.idiomatic: All Shu united in praise of him.

sentences.zh: 元起舅子梁矜孫性輕脫，與黔婁志行不同，乃言於元起曰：「城中稱有三刺史，節下何以堪之！

translations.literal: Yuanqi's nephew-by-marriage Liang Jinsun was frivolous by nature and differed from Qianlou in aim and conduct; he therefore said to Yuanqi: "Within the city they speak of three provincial inspectors—how can Your Lordship bear it!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi's nephew Liang Jinsun was flighty and at odds with Qianlou in character; he told Yuanqi, "The city calls this place ruled by three inspectors—how can you endure it!

sentences.zh: 」元起由此疏黔屢、光濟，而治迹稍損。

translations.literal: 」 From this Yuanqi grew distant toward Qianlou and Guangji, and his record in office slightly declined.
translations.idiomatic: From that Yuanqi distanced Qianlou and Guangji, and his governance slackened.

sentences.zh: 在州二年，以母老乞歸供養，詔許焉。

translations.literal: After two years in the province, because his mother was old he begged leave to return and support her; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in the province his mother's age moved him to ask to go home and care for her; the court assented.

sentences.zh: 徵爲右衛將軍，以西昌侯蕭淵藻代之。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Right Guard General, and Marquis of Xichang Xiao Yuanzao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Right Guard General, and Marquis of Xichang Xiao Yuanzao took his place.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁州長史夏侯道遷以南鄭叛，引魏人，白馬戍主尹天寶馳使報蜀，魏將王景胤、孔陵寇東西晉壽，並遣告急，衆勸元起急救之。

translations.literal: At this time Liangzhou Chief Clerk Xiahou Daqian rebelled at Nanzheng and brought in Wei troops; White Horse Garrison Commander Yin Tianbao sent riders posthaste to report to Shu; Wei generals Wang Jingyin and Kong Ling raided Eastern and Western Jinshou, all sending urgent appeals; the multitude urged Yuanqi to rush to their relief.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liangzhou chief clerk Xiahou Daqian turned Nanzheng over to Wei; Yin Tianbao of White Horse Garrison galloped word to Shu; Wang Jingyin and Kong Ling of Wei attacked the two Jinshou posts and all cried for help; many pressed Yuanqi to march at once.

sentences.zh: 元起曰：「朝廷萬里，軍不卒至，若寇賊侵淫，方須撲討，董督之任，非我而誰？

translations.literal: Yuanqi said: "The court is ten thousand li away; troops cannot arrive at once. If bandits spread their harm, then it will be time to strike them down—the duty to oversee and suppress, whose if not mine?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi said, "The court is ten thousand li off; armies cannot come overnight. If the enemy spreads, then we must beat them back—the task of command, who but me?

sentences.zh: 何事匆匆便救。

translations.literal: Why rush off at once to rescue them?
translations.idiomatic: Why hurry to rescue them now?

sentences.zh: 」黔婁等苦諫之，皆不從。

translations.literal: 」 Qianlou and the others earnestly remonstrated, but he would not listen to any.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlou and the rest pleaded hard, but he would hear none of it.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦假元起節，都督征討諸軍事，救漢中。

translations.literal: Gaozu also lent Yuanqi credentials, making him regional commander of punitive campaign military affairs, to rescue Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu also gave Yuanqi the staff and made him commander of the punitive forces to relieve Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 比至，魏已攻陷兩晉壽。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Wei had already taken both Jinshou posts.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Wei had already overrun both Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 淵藻將至。

translations.literal: Yuanzao was about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzao was nearing.

sentences.zh: 元起頗營還裝，糧儲器械，略無遺者。

translations.literal: Yuanqi went to some lengths preparing his return baggage; grain stores, equipment, and weapons—almost nothing was left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi busied himself packing for the return; grain, stores, and arms—hardly anything remained.

sentences.zh: 淵藻入城，甚怨望之，因表其逗留不憂軍事。

translations.literal: Yuanzao entered the city and deeply resented him; he thereupon memorialized that Yuanqi had delayed and showed no concern for military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzao entered the city full of grievance and memorialized that Yuanqi had lingered and neglected the army.

sentences.zh: 收付州獄，於獄自縊，時年四十八。

translations.literal: He was taken into the provincial prison; in prison he hanged himself, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was committed to the provincial jail and hanged himself there, aged forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 有司追劾削爵土，詔減邑之半，乃更封松滋縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: The authorities pursued impeachment and stripped his noble land; an edict reduced his fief by half, then re-enfeoffed him as Marquis of Songzi district with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The offices pursued charges and stripped his fief; an edict halved his estate, then made him Marquis of Songzi with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 初，元起在荊州，刺史隨王板元起爲從事，別駕庾蓽堅執不可，元起恨之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuanqi was in Jing province, the Prince of Sui as inspector had Yuanqi appointed as aide, but Registrar Yu Bi firmly refused and would not allow it—Yuanqi resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Jingzhou the Prince of Sui had posted Yuanqi as aide, but registrar Yu Bi stood firm against it, and Yuanqi bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 大軍旣至京師，蓽在城內，甚懼。

translations.literal: When the great army had reached the capital, Bi was inside the city and greatly feared.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force reached the capital, Bi was within the walls and terrified.

sentences.zh: 及城平，元起先遣迎蓽，語人曰：「庾別駕若爲亂兵所殺，我無以自明。

translations.literal: When the city was pacified, Yuanqi first sent men to welcome Bi, telling others: "If Registrar Yu Bi were killed by disorderly troops, I could not clear myself."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Yuanqi sent first to receive Bi and told people, "If Registrar Yu Bi were killed in the turmoil, I could never prove my innocence."

sentences.zh: 」因厚遣之。

translations.literal: 」 He therefore sent him away with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Bi off with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 少時又嘗至其西沮田舍，有沙門造之乞，元起問田人曰：「有稻幾何？

translations.literal: In youth he once went to his Xiju farmstead; a monk came to beg of him; Yuanqi asked the farmer: "How much rice do you have?
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he once visited his farm at Xiju; a monk came begging; Yuanqi asked the farmer, "How much rice is there?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「二十斛。

translations.literal: 」 The reply came: "Twenty hu."
translations.idiomatic: The answer was, "Twenty hu."

sentences.zh: 」元起悉以施之。

translations.literal: 」 Yuanqi gave it all away.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi gave the whole amount away.

sentences.zh: 時人稱其有大度。

translations.literal: People of the time praised his great magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the day praised his largeness of spirit.

sentences.zh: 元起初爲益州，過江陵迎其母，母事道，方居館，不肯出。

translations.literal: When Yuanqi first went to Yizhou, he crossed through Jiangling to fetch his mother; his mother practiced the Way and was then living in a lodge, and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanqi first took Yizhou he passed Jiangling to bring his mother; she followed the Way and was in a lodge, and refused to leave it.

sentences.zh: 元起拜請同行。

translations.literal: Yuanqi bowed and begged her to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi bowed and pleaded that she come with him.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「貧賤家兒忽得富貴，詎可久保，我寧死不能與汝共入禍敗。

translations.literal: His mother said: "A poor family's son who suddenly gains wealth—how can it long be kept? I would rather die than enter ruin with you.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "A poor boy who suddenly grows rich cannot keep it long; I would rather die than share your downfall.

sentences.zh: 」元起之至巴東，聞蜀亂，使蔣光濟筮之，遇《蹇》，喟然歎曰：「吾豈鄧艾而及此乎。

translations.literal: 」 When Yuanqi reached Badong and heard of turmoil in Shu, he had Jiang Guangji cast the divination sticks; they produced the hexagram Jian; he sighed and said: "Am I a Deng Ai, that I should come to this?
translations.idiomatic: At Badong he heard Shu was in revolt and had Jiang Guangji divine; the hexagram was Jian; he sighed, "Am I Deng Ai, to meet such an end?

sentences.zh: 」後果如筮。

translations.literal: 」 In the end it turned out just as the divination had indicated.
translations.idiomatic: In the end all came to pass as the divination foretold.

sentences.zh: 子鏗嗣。

translations.literal: His son Keng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Keng inherited.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：永元之末，荊州方未有釁，蕭穎胄悉全楚之兵，首應義舉。

translations.literal: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: At the end of Yongyuan, Jing province had still no sign of trouble; Xiao Yingchen mustered all Chu's troops and was first to answer the righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha said: In late Yongyuan Jingzhou had not yet stirred; Xiao Yingchen gathered all Chu's forces and led the response to the righteous cause.

sentences.zh: 豈天之所啓，人惎之謀？

translations.literal: Was it Heaven's opening, or men's stirring counsel?
translations.idiomatic: Was it Heaven's prompting, or human design?

sentences.zh: 不然，何其響附之決也？

translations.literal: If not, how could their swift rallying be so decisive?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise how could men have rallied so swiftly and so surely?

sentences.zh: 穎達叔侄慶流後嗣，夏侯、楊、鄧咸享隆名，盛矣！

translations.literal: Yingda and his uncle and nephew—blessings flowed to later generations; Xiahou, Yang, and Deng all enjoyed lofty fame—magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Yingda and his kin reaped fortune for their heirs; Xiahou, Yang, and Deng all won great renown—splendid!

sentences.zh: 詳之謹厚，楊、蔡廉節，君子有取焉。

translations.literal: Xiang's care and solidity, Yang and Cai's integrity—gentlemen may take them as models.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's prudence and weight, Yang and Cai's clean conduct—men of worth may esteem them.
